_about: Lessons & classes and the teaching pictures. Each lesson lists its parts (file paths in the repo), its doctrine topics (ids from topics.json), the chapters it teaches on ("Genesis 3") and key verses. Edit freely, then run python3 tools/build_lessons.py.

shelves.name: The Doctrine class
shelves.about: A Sunday class on the fundamentals of the faith, week by week, with slides, notes, worksheets and answer keys.

shelves.name: Doctrine by topic
shelves.about: Slide decks on each doctrine, built from the teachings filed under it, with links back to those teachings.

shelves.name: Genesis class
shelves.about: Slides for the Genesis class, chapter by chapter.

shelves.name: Romans class
shelves.about: Slides for the Sunday class through Romans, week by week.

shelves.name: Bible lessons
shelves.about: Lessons from John, the Psalms, Proverbs and the epistles, and a start for new believers.

shelves.name: Sermons
shelves.about: Sermons preached from the pulpit, from the notes they were preached from.

shelves.name: Standalone posts
shelves.about: Teachings posted on their own on the Jag's 2.0 and 3.0 channels (2021–22), outside the chapter studies.

shelves.name: Answering error
shelves.about: Calvinism, Catholicism, falling away, dispensational error and vain philosophy, answered from scripture.

shelves.name: Baptist & church history
shelves.about: The line of believers through history, the early writings, and the preserved Word: history to learn from, not a system to be married to.

shelves.name: Prophecy & the covenants
shelves.about: Daniel, the order of the end times, and God's conditional promises.

shelves.name: From other preachers
shelves.about: Material from other men, kept for reference. Compare it with scripture like everything else.

lessons.title: Week 1: The Importance of Doctrine
lessons.summary: Gives five reasons the Word gives for holding fast sound doctrine: to know God's will, gain wisdom, teach others, recognize false ways, and be of one mind with believers. The notes and study guide add Jesus' own doctrine from the Father, and the worksheet has fill-in-the-blank verses.

lessons.title: Week 2: How God Reveals Himself to Man
lessons.summary: Distinguishes general revelation (creation and conscience) from specific revelation (the Word, the prophets, and Jesus Christ). Looks at how God makes Himself known through creation, wrath, mercy, and Scripture.

lessons.title: Week 3: The Doctrine of Scripture
lessons.summary: Teaches the inspiration, preservation, and inerrancy of Scripture, and why all doctrine must come from clear Scripture. Closes with what an every-word Bible means for the believer.

lessons.title: Shadows and Substance: Why the Old Testament Practices
lessons.summary: Shows that the Tabernacle, sacrifices, and washings were shadows that sanctified the flesh and pointed to Christ, while righteousness has always come by faith. One deck covers the subject, ending with the new heaven where God and the Lamb are the temple.

lessons.title: The Epistles Placed in the Book of Acts
lessons.summary: Lists the epistles in the order they were most likely written, set against the chapters of Acts, followed by the post-Acts epistles and Revelation. Serves as a reading guide for placing each letter in its setting.

lessons.title: Week 4: The Importance of the KJV
lessons.summary: Traces how God preserved His Word in English, from Tyndale's martyrdom to the translators of 1611 and the KJV's lasting legacy. Handouts include fun Bible facts, a KJV pronoun chart (thou and ye), a study guide on engaging with God's Word, and a review sheet with answer key.

lessons.title: "Are Saved" or "Being Saved"? 1 Corinthians 1:18 and 15:2
lessons.summary: Looks at the Greek participle in 1 Corinthians 1:18 and why the KJV's "are saved" fits the settled work of God, compared with the modern "being saved." Connects the wording to eternal security.

lessons.title: Week 5: A Trail of Blood and Being Baptist
lessons.summary: A brief history of the Baptists: a line of believers, not a chain of churches, who held the Bible’s distinctives in every age at the cost of their blood; the great splits of Christendom; Mystery, Babylon; and the B.A.P.T.I.S.T. distinctives, with the worksheet and answer key.

lessons.title: Week 6: Terms and Conditions
lessons.summary: Defines the working vocabulary of the faith, such as grace, faith, repentance, the Godhead, and salvation, with Scripture for each term. Groups the terms under how we are saved, the Godhead, the Christian life, the end times, and rightly dividing.

lessons.title: Week 7: The Doctrine of God (the Father)
lessons.summary: Studies the nature and attributes of God the Father, the seven Spirits of God, the seven things God hates, and the names of God. Considers the Godhead.

lessons.title: Week 8: The Doctrine of Christ
lessons.summary: Presents Jesus as promised, pre-incarnate, Creator, eternal Son, fully God and fully man, and the only way of salvation. Includes the Old Testament theophanies, the seven I Am statements, and a match-the-verse worksheet.

lessons.title: That Rock Was Christ, Not Peter
lessons.summary: Looks at Matthew 16:18 and quotes early church writers such as Origen, Chrysostom, Hilary, Ambrose, and Augustine to show that the rock is Christ and the faith of Peter's confession, not Peter.

lessons.title: Week 9: The Doctrine of the Holy Spirit
lessons.summary: Studies the Comforter, His deity, His work in convicting the world, and His role in salvation and sanctification. Also covers gifts, fruit, and blasphemy against the Holy Ghost.

lessons.title: Week 10: Marriage, God's Plan for Man and Woman
lessons.summary: Follows marriage from God's design in Eden through His view of divorce and adultery under the Law to the marriage supper at the end of all things.

lessons.title: Outline of the Covenants: Rightly Dividing
lessons.summary: Sets out a framework in which many Old Testament promises were conditional on Israel's obedience, traced through a timeline from Genesis to the prophets. Explains how the New Testament presents the fulfillment under the new covenant.

lessons.title: Fundamental Doctrine Outline
lessons.summary: Gives the full outline of the doctrine class in numbered parts, from the importance of doctrine and Scripture through God, ordinances, the new man, heaven, hell, and soul winning. Lists key verses for each point.

lessons.title: Genesis 1: Creation
lessons.summary: Goes through the six days of creation verse by verse, with cross references on the Word and Spirit at creation.

lessons.title: Genesis 2: Marriage
lessons.summary: Walks through Genesis 2, from the Sabbath and the formation of man to God's design for marriage as one flesh.

lessons.title: Genesis 2: Marriage and Divorce
lessons.summary: Shows God's original design for marriage and examines what Malachi, the Sermon on the Mount, and Matthew 19 say about divorce.

lessons.title: Genesis 3: The Fall
lessons.summary: Walks through the serpent's question, the fall of Eve and Adam, the curse, and the first promise of a Redeemer.

lessons.title: Genesis 4: Cain and Abel
lessons.summary: Looks at the two offerings, God's warning to Cain, the first murder, and the line that began to call on the LORD.

lessons.title: Genesis 5: The Generations of Adam
lessons.summary: Reads the genealogy from Adam to Noah as literal history, noting that Adam's own likeness was passed to Seth.

lessons.title: Genesis 6: The Days of Noah
lessons.summary: How short the time was from the garden to the Flood, and how far man fell: wickedness only evil continually, God's grief and judgment, and Noah finding grace and walking with God by faith. As the days of Noah were, so shall the coming of the Son of man be.

lessons.title: Genesis 6: Sons of God
lessons.summary: Who were the sons of God who took the daughters of men? Both views stated fairly, the believers of Seth's line and fallen angels, then compared text by text from the King James Bible: the two lines of Cain and Seth, the giants, and whether God would call fallen angels His sons.

lessons.title: Genesis 7: The Flood
lessons.summary: Built from the Genesis 7 study: Noah called into the ark, the Lord shutting him in, the windows of heaven and fountains of the deep, and all flesh dying in a global flood. The Bible says it’s true, and that’s enough; scoffers are willingly ignorant, and believers stand ready with an answer, like Noah.

lessons.title: Creation Ex Nihilo
lessons.summary: Defends creation out of nothing and answers the Divine Council theory of Michael Heiser from John 1, Colossians 1, Hebrews 11, and Genesis. Holds that God made all things alone by His Word.

lessons.title: Fundamentalism vs. Vain Philosophy
lessons.summary: Shows that where Scripture presents mystery, the fundamentalist stops, while the philosopher and theologian press on and answer heresy with counter-heresy. Traces the back-and-forth of early church controversy and rests on the witness of God in 1 John 5 and the warning of Colossians 2.

lessons.title: Wise as Serpents
lessons.summary: A Sunday School lesson on Matthew 10:16 and the two charges Jesus gives, to be wise as serpents and harmless as doves. Warns against the dove-only trap and looks at handling doubtful disputations and sowers of division.

lessons.title: Believers Cannot Apostatize and Apostates Cannot Believe
lessons.summary: Starts from Romans 1:18-23 to show that men who know the truth and hold it in unrighteousness are given up to a reprobate mind. Argues that a true believer is kept and that those who fall away were never saved.

lessons.title: Against Mid-Acts Dispensationalism (Acts 15:8-11)
lessons.summary: Answers the Mid-Acts claim of a different gospel for the Gentiles from Acts 15:8-11. Shows that Peter held the same gospel of grace as Paul and that men from Adam on have been saved by grace through faith.

lessons.title: Romans 9
lessons.summary: Reads Romans 9 in the context of Israel, showing God's mercy to the nations through the gospel and the hardening of unbelieving Israel, rather than individuals chosen for heaven or hell.

lessons.title: A Fundamentalist View on Atonement, Salvation and Election
lessons.summary: Sets out a plain-reading view of the atonement as Christ's propitiatory death, cosmic in scope and offered to all, with salvation received by faith. Keeps God's sovereignty and human responsibility together without leaning on Calvinism or Arminianism.

lessons.title: The Biblical Doctrine of Reconciliation and Atonement
lessons.summary: An outline beginning at Luke 2 on reconciliation through Christ's blood, distinguishing atonement as the means from reconciliation as the result. Presents the reconciliation as objective and wide in scope, with personal salvation received by faith and kept secure.

lessons.title: The TULIP Trap: Rejecting Calvinist and Arminian Premises
lessons.summary: A planned four-to-six lesson series outline arguing that the TULIP debate rests on faulty premises. Goes through the points one at a time, affirming what Scripture says while rejecting the Calvinist and Arminian framework.

lessons.title: Augustine and Pelagius
lessons.summary: Looks at the early fifth-century clash between Augustine and Pelagius as a turning point in how grace and the human will came to be taught. Argues that Augustine's views, carried into the Roman church, are the root of later Calvinist and Arminian systems.

lessons.title: Election in the Bible
lessons.summary: A table of how Scripture uses election, for Israel, angels, Christ and believers, each with its purpose, conditions and what cuts off. Shows election as being singled out for service, privilege and holiness rather than God choosing who will believe.

lessons.title: The Biblical Truth About Perseverance of the Saints
lessons.summary: Starts with the question of how a person knows he is saved and compares Calvinist and Arminian teaching on perseverance. Contrasts both with the Bible's eternal life promised by a God who cannot lie, so that believers may know they have it.

lessons.title: John R. Rice on Election
lessons.summary: Gives background on Calvinism and Arminianism and then sets out John R. Rice's teaching on unlimited atonement, whosoever-will salvation and election. Closes with the biblical fundamentalist view of election as a call to service and holiness.

lessons.title: Expository: James 2:14-17
lessons.summary: A short draft exposition reading James 2 as written to saved Christians, urging faith to be shown in serving others. Notes that works justify a man before men, not before God.

lessons.title: The Didache
lessons.summary: Walks through the Didache, the first-century Teaching of the Twelve, as a witness to early church practice and not as Scripture. Covers its date, rediscovery and contents, always measured by the KJV.

lessons.title: Ignatius and the Lord's Table
lessons.summary: Answers the Catholic transubstantiation proof text in Ignatius, Smyrnaeans 7:1, in its own context. Shows that Ignatius was fighting the Docetists, who denied Christ came in the flesh, and measures him by the KJV.

lessons.title: Baptist Voices
lessons.summary: Gathers quotations from Jack Hyles, John R. Rice and others of the twentieth century fundamentalist movement who said plainly that they were Baptists. Follows the earlier study of Baptist names through history.

lessons.title: Baptist Names in History
lessons.summary: Traces the many names worn by the people of God from Antioch onward, such as Novatianists and Cathari. Shows the same conviction beneath each, that a church is a company of the saved baptized upon profession of faith.

lessons.title: Baptist Groups Compared
lessons.summary: Compares Independent Fundamental, Particular (Calvinist) and Arminian-leaning Baptists on grace through faith, eternal security, free response and the Baptist distinctives. Uses the IFB position as the baseline.

lessons.title: Saint Patrick Was a Baptist
lessons.summary: A ministry essay presenting Patrick as a missionary sent from an independent church in Britain. Quotes his Confessio on salvation by grace through faith.

lessons.title: Relics Heresy: Vigilantius vs. Jerome
lessons.summary: Looks at the debate around 406 AD between Vigilantius and Jerome over relic veneration, night vigils and praying to saints. Presents Vigilantius as holding to Scripture against creeping pagan customs.

lessons.title: Early American Baptists: Establishment, Disestablishment and Soul Liberty
lessons.summary: New England and Southern Baptists such as Roger Williams, John Clarke, Obadiah Holmes, Isaac Backus and John Leland. Covers what they fought, including tax-funded churches and licensing laws, and what they argued for, soul liberty and believer's baptism, with the middle way between them, through to the First Amendment.

lessons.title: Daniel Merrill, A Forgotten Baptist
lessons.summary: Tells how Daniel Merrill, a Congregational pastor in Sedgwick, Maine, studied baptism and became a Baptist in 1805. Notes his firm later writings on baptized church membership.

lessons.title: Dispensationalism, an Enemy of Soul Winning
lessons.summary: An excerpt from Jack Hyles, Enemies of Soul Winning, chapter 2, on ultra-dispensationalism. Holds that salvation has always been by grace through faith and answers the Scofield footnote on legal obedience.

lessons.title: Baptist Perpetuity
lessons.summary: Gathers quotations from historians and even opponents, including Mosheim and Cardinal Hosius, on Baptist-like churches existing through the centuries. Supports the succession of New Testament churches apart from Rome.

lessons.title: I Reject the Nicene Creed
lessons.summary: Explains why the author rejects the Nicene Creed, holding that its Greek terms such as begotten and homoousios brought new errors in answering Arianism. Stands on the Godhead as stated in Scripture alone.

lessons.title: Amazing Grace
lessons.summary: A short devotional on the hymn written by John Newton in 1772 and what it says of God's grace to a wretch. Reflects on grace shown even now.

lessons.title: The Single Gospel Through-Line in American Evangelicalism
lessons.summary: A brief outline following one gospel of grace through faith alone from the Great Awakenings through later American evangelicalism. Shows its preservation in the IFB tradition.

lessons.title: Obadiah Holmes: A Testimony of Perseverance in Christ
lessons.summary: Tells the life of Obadiah Holmes, from his youth in Lancashire to his conversion and Baptist convictions. Recounts the steadfast faith he showed under persecution in New England.

lessons.title: The Septuagint Myth
lessons.summary: Argues against the traditional account of a second-century BC Septuagint, beginning with the Letter of Aristeas. Defends the preserved Hebrew Masoretic Text and the Byzantine text behind the KJV.

lessons.title: The Apocrypha
lessons.summary: Shows from Christ's own words about the Old Testament canon why the Apocrypha is not Scripture. Treats the law, prophets and psalms as the whole canon Jesus taught.

lessons.title: Daniel 11
lessons.summary: A verse-by-verse study of Daniel 11 from the Persian kings to Antiochus Epiphanes, matched to history from 533 to 164 BC. Notes that it also foreshadows the end-times Antichrist and the events of Daniel 12.

lessons.title: Conditional Promises and Covenant Shifts
lessons.summary: Presents a rightly dividing framework in which Old Testament kingdom promises were conditional on Israel's obedience. Shows the New Testament as a reconfigured, spiritual fulfillment under the new covenant, with salvation always by grace through faith.

lessons.title: Timeline of Days in Daniel 8 and 12
lessons.summary: Lays out the 2,300, 1,290 and 1,335 days of Daniel 8 and 12 within the seven-year week of Daniel 9:27. Divides the period into its two halves.

lessons.title: Conditional Covenants and the Forfeited Promises of Ezekiel's Temple
lessons.summary: A book-by-book look at conditional and unconditional promises in Scripture, with human choices and changed outcomes. Distinguishes individual judgment by faith from national judgment by works.

lessons.title: OT Prophecy: God's Grace in a Conditional Promise
lessons.summary: Shows the conditional nature of Ezekiel's temple vision as God's grace, an offered chance of national repentance despite His foreknowledge. Connects it to the Mosaic covenant.

lessons.title: The Book of Revelation: Daniel's 70th Week (chart)
lessons.summary: A timeline chart placing the seals, trumpets and vials of Revelation within Daniel's seventieth week, from Faithful Word Baptist Church.

lessons.title: Post-Tribulation, Pre-Wrath Timeline
lessons.summary: Sets out a post-tribulation, pre-wrath timeline in Daniel's seven-year week, with general tribulation, a 75-day great tribulation and then God's wrath. Reads Revelation as two parallel accounts and has the church present through the tribulation.

lessons.title: John 6: The Bread of Life
lessons.summary: A plain reading of John 6:26-71 showing that Jesus interprets the bread and the eating and drinking as coming to Him and believing on Him. Follows the discourse from the rebuke to Peter's confession.

lessons.title: John: That Ye Might Believe
lessons.summary: Traces the gospel of John chapter by chapter through its figures, dark sayings and dual phrasings. Shows that every figure restates John 3:16 and that the book was written that ye might believe.

lessons.title: The Old Testament in Light of the New: Stephen
lessons.summary: Retells Old Testament history as one story with many witnesses, following Stephen's account and similar surveys such as Nehemiah 9. Reads it with the New Testament's own explanation.

lessons.title: So You're a Saved Christian, Now What?
lessons.summary: A seven-session study for new believers on the gospel, baptism, witnessing, prayer, Bible study, a life that pleases God and the hope of glory. Begins by rooting assurance in Christ's finished work.

lessons.title: The Words of God: Jack Hyles on Inspiration
lessons.summary: A short slide lesson from Jack Hyles on the inspiration of Scripture, with God as the Penman and men as pens. Argues that a perfect, preserved English Bible makes all the difference.

lessons.title: Psalm 22: A Cry from the Cross
lessons.summary: Reads Psalm 22 as David's prophetic song that Christ prayed from the cross, with tap-to-see notes on how verses point to Calvary.

lessons.title: Psalm 50: God Is Judge
lessons.summary: Reads Psalm 50 as a courtroom in four movements: the summons, the sacrifice God seeks, the indictment and the verdict. Applies the case against His people to us.

lessons.title: 2 Peter 2:19-22 Notes
lessons.summary: Notes on the false teachers of 2 Peter 2:19-22 who promise liberty while enslaved to sin. Compares readings of the passage and the Balaam connection, including the warning of lost fellowship and discipline for a believer.

lessons.title: Spiritual Father
lessons.summary: A Father's Day message honoring the pastor who led the author to Christ. The author tells how he went from a Catholic upbringing with no assurance to hearing the Romans Road and trusting Christ.

lessons.title: Proverbs: Instruction to the Heirs of the Kingdom
lessons.summary: An overview of the book of Proverbs as Solomon's instruction to his son. It covers raising children in the fear of the LORD, Lady Wisdom against the strange woman, the gospel promises in Proverbs, and its counsel for the princes of the Kingdom.

lessons.title: New Year, New Man
lessons.summary: Looks at New Year's resolutions in light of the Bible. It warns against rash worldly vows and gives godly principles: forget the past, commit everything to the Lord, and make practical resolutions such as daily Bible reading, prayer, gratitude, witnessing and service.

lessons.title: In Defense of Christmas
lessons.summary: Explains that Jeremiah 10 is about carved and gilded idols and is not a prohibition of the Christmas tree. It answers common objections about the date and name of Christmas, and calls on believers to be fully persuaded in their own minds and to celebrate the birth of Christ.

lessons.title: Increase Our Faith
lessons.summary: Shows from Luke 17 that when the apostles asked for more faith, the Lord pointed them to obedience first. Applies the point to forgiving, honoring parents, marriage, work, church attendance and soul winning, and ends with an invitation to take the first step of trusting Christ.

lessons.title: Haggai the Prophet
lessons.summary: Walks through Haggai's short ministry to the returned exiles, calling them to rebuild the temple. Notes that Zerubbabel is in the line of David that leads to Christ, and encourages believers to build up the local church.

lessons.title: Faith Over Fear
lessons.summary: Encourages believers to put faith in the Lord over the fears of the world, while keeping a right fear of the LORD. Draws on the author's own nerves about preaching and soul winning, and on God's promise to be with His people.

lessons.title: Embracing Hope
lessons.summary: Follows Simeon, who embraced the child Jesus, as an Old Testament saint who waited in hope. It points to the faith of Hebrews 11 and the blessed hope of the resurrection and the rapture.

lessons.title: Watch
lessons.summary: Uses Simeon and Anna and the Hebrews 11 saints as examples of those who watched for redemption. Calls believers to watch and wait for Christ's return, redeeming the time by warning and winning souls.

lessons.title: Help Me, Help You
lessons.summary: Presents helping others as a gift of God, a commandment of God and a promise of God. Teaches that charity is love in action and gives practical ways to serve at home, church and work.

lessons.title: The Gift of Helps
lessons.summary: Looks at 1 Corinthians 12 and the less showy gift of helps as equal in the body of Christ. Urges believers to seek that gift and to serve the church and others with charity.

lessons.title: Are You Persuaded?
lessons.summary: Starts from Agrippa's "Almost thou persuadest me" and asks what it takes to be persuaded of the truth. Sets out the scriptural witnesses to Christ and the martyrs and saints who were persuaded unto death, ending with Paul's persuasion in Romans 8.

lessons.title: Peter Went Out, and Wept Bitterly
lessons.summary: Takes Peter's denial of Christ and his restoration at the sea of Tiberias as an encouragement for believers who regret missed chances to share the gospel. Shows Peter's later boldness and his epistles' counsel to stand against scoffers.

lessons.title: Taming Your Tongue
lessons.summary: Gathers what the Bible says about the tongue, from James 3 and Proverbs. It warns against vulgarity, swearing, gossip and talebearing, and urges using the tongue to praise God, edify others and share the gospel.

lessons.title: Psalm 32: The Blessedness of Forgiveness
lessons.summary: A Wednesday night study of David's psalm on forgiveness, tied to Paul's use of it in Romans 4. Walks through confession and God's mercy to the forgiven believer, with a deeper study of the words transgression, sin and iniquity.

lessons.title: The "good person" lie
lessons.summary: Shows that Satan promotes the idea that being moral makes a man righteous, when Scripture says none is righteous and all have sinned. Warns that self-righteousness leaves people open to strong delusion.

lessons.title: Abraham saved by faith alone, and James 2
lessons.summary: Argues from Genesis 15:6 and Romans 4 that Abraham was saved by faith decades before he offered Isaac, so James 2 speaks of justification before men. Warns that any teacher adding works to salvation preaches another gospel.

lessons.title: No limbo and no purgatory
lessons.summary: Says Jesus did not go to limbo to free the just, since none are righteous apart from faith in Christ. Teaches there is only heaven and hell, and that Abraham's bosom is a place of comfort in heaven.

lessons.title: You can know where you are going
lessons.summary: Teaches that a believer can know with certainty that he has eternal life by trusting Christ's finished work alone. Closes with 1 John 5:13-15.

lessons.title: The gift received, or rejected until reprobate
lessons.summary: Describes salvation received by faith by calling on the Lord since Seth, and those who willfully reject it being turned over by God to a reprobate mind.

lessons.title: Faith in Christ first, not in science
lessons.summary: Urges Christians to rest their faith in Christ and the grace of God the Creator rather than in science and history. Cites 1 Corinthians 1:22-24 and Hebrews 11:1.

lessons.title: Subject to the Higher Powers: Romans 13 and the Christian
lessons.summary: Posts on being subject to the powers ordained of God, rendering to Caesar and to God, Paul's example in chains, and turning to God rather than to politics or violence.

lessons.title: Liberty Comes from Christ: Why Nations Rise and Fall
lessons.summary: Posts teaching that liberty comes from Christ, that God judges nations by their works, and that the means of government is incidental to the hearts of the people.

lessons.title: Why We Keep the King James Bible
lessons.summary: Posts contrasting a modern paraphrase of John 6 with the KJV, rejecting the critical text, and teaching scripture alone from Leviticus 10.

lessons.title: Israel Put Away: The Bill of Divorcement
lessons.summary: Posts from the channel on Matthew 28, 1 Thessalonians 2, Ezekiel 16 and Jeremiah 3 about unbelieving Israel put away with a bill of divorcement and the new wife sealed by the Spirit.

lessons.title: Received Ye the Spirit by Works?
lessons.summary: Posts from the channel comparing the "repent of your sins" gospel to the Galatian error of being made perfect by the flesh, with salvation by believing on the Son.

lessons.title: Fear of Man or Fear of God: Zedekiah and Jeremiah
lessons.summary: Posts from the channel on Jeremiah 38 about speaking boldly though mocked, King Zedekiah's fear of man, and setting our minds on Christ rather than waiting on a leader.

lessons.title: Romans: Who Is Paul, and How Romans Argues
lessons.summary: Opens the Romans class with who the apostle Paul was, and how the epistle is built as one logical argument in the diatribe style.

lessons.title: Romans 1: The Wrath of God Revealed
lessons.summary: Romans 1:18-32 as the logical progression of God's wrath on those who hold the truth in unrighteousness, with the review sheet for weeks 1 and 2.

lessons.title: Romans 2: The Inescapable Judgment
lessons.summary: Romans 2:1-11 on the judgment of God that no man escapes, Jew or Gentile, by judging others.

lessons.title: Romans 3: All Are Guilty, Saved by Grace
lessons.summary: The oracles of God prove all are guilty, God's plan for the heathen in the Old Testament, and salvation as a finished work by grace through faith.

lessons.title: Romans 4: Abraham Believed God
lessons.summary: Abraham believed God and it was counted for righteousness, with the lineage from Adam to the twelve tribes.

lessons.title: Romans 5: Peace and Grace
lessons.summary: Peace with God through justification by faith, atonement and reconciliation, the fall in Genesis 3 as its background, and the key verses on justification.

lessons.title: Romans 6: Dead to Sin, Alive in Christ
lessons.summary: Dead to sin and alive unto God, baptism into Christ, servants of sin or of righteousness, with a recap of Romans 1-5 and a worksheet.

lessons.title: Romans 7: The Struggle with Sin
lessons.summary: The law, the age of accountability, and the old man against the new: O wretched man that I am.

lessons.title: Romans 8: No Condemnation
lessons.summary: No condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus, life in the Spirit, and nothing able to separate us from the love of God. The election chart for this week is on the Answering error shelf.

lessons.title: Romans 9: God's Word Has Not Failed
lessons.summary: Romans 9 on the children of the promise: Jacob and Esau, God choosing the weak and foolish, the parallel in Galatians 3-4, and a recap of Romans 1-8.

lessons.title: Romans 10: Salvation by Faith
lessons.summary: The righteousness which is of faith, confessing and believing, and the call to soul winning: how shall they hear without a preacher?

lessons.title: Romans 11: God's Mercy and Faithfulness
lessons.summary: Paul's heart for unbelieving Israel, one people of God from Adam to Christ, dispensation as stewardship, and a summary of Romans 9-11 as one argument.

lessons.title: Romans 12: A Living Sacrifice
lessons.summary: Present your bodies a living sacrifice, be transformed by the renewing of your mind, and serve one another in love.

lessons.title: Romans 13: Subject to the Higher Powers
lessons.summary: Submitting to God-given authority, Daniel's faithful refusal of the king's meat as its limit, and love as the fulfilling of the law.

lessons.title: Romans 14: Receive One Another
lessons.summary: Receiving the weak in faith, the liberty in Christ, and the warning that a little leaven leavens the whole lump.

lessons.title: Romans 15: Unity, Edification and Hope
lessons.summary: Bearing the infirmities of the weak, and the Old Testament prophecies of the Gentiles glorifying God that Christ came to fulfil.

lessons.title: Romans 16: Greetings, Warnings and the Doxology
lessons.summary: The saints Paul greets by name and what history tells of them, the warning to mark and avoid them which cause divisions, and the closing doxology.

lessons.title: Brother Mark and His Lies
lessons.summary: Judge righteous judgment, not by appearance: Job's friends, respect of persons, and suffering that is chastening, for God's glory, or just time and chance. Then, in fun, a defense of Lazarus the beggar against a brother's sermon, closing on Romans 14 and loving brethren who differ on secondary things.

lessons.title: Saved by Grace Through Faith
lessons.summary: Saved by grace through faith in Christ, without works. This is the Gospel. There is nothing more to it. There can be nothing less.

lessons.title: Grace, Not Works
lessons.summary: Grace is the unearned, unmerited, undeserved gift given by God from His mercy and love. Salvation by grace through faith without works has been the Gospel from the beginning.

lessons.title: Imputed Righteousness
lessons.summary: Jesus took on our sin and paid the price for all of it. By believing this, we take on His righteousness: it is an exchange, and God will not impute sin to the man that believeth.

lessons.title: Repentance Is a Change of Mind
lessons.summary: Repentance means a change of heart, to believe something that we hadn't before. It is turning from false beliefs to God and believing His word, not turning from sins to be saved.

lessons.title: All Have Sinned
lessons.summary: We are all sinners before a holy God. All are under sin, all deserve death and Hell, all need salvation, and none have any excuse.

lessons.title: Repentance and Assurance
lessons.summary: Godly sorrow, confession, and the believer kept by God. Repent means to change your mind, and once you are saved you are always saved, always His, always His sheep.

lessons.title: Eternal Security
lessons.summary: If a person has believed in their heart that Jesus Christ died for their sins, they can NEVER lose their salvation. Once saved always saved is not just a slogan, it is the truth of the Gospel.

lessons.title: Sealed by the Spirit
lessons.summary: Once we believe we are sealed by the Holy Spirit as the earnest, the down payment as it were, until redemption. The only surety we can count on is God's.

lessons.title: Confession and Forgiveness
lessons.summary: First John is written to the saved: if we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive. God wants to forgive us more than we want to be forgiven.

lessons.title: Chastened as Sons
lessons.summary: God chastises His own for our iniquity. He takes the rod to His children when they sin, sometimes very harshly, sometimes with death, yet He puts away their sin and they are still saved.

lessons.title: Godly Sorrow Worketh Repentance
lessons.summary: Godly sorrow, sincerely being sorry at a wrong you've done, leads many to the repentance of belief that is salvation, while the sorrow of this world works death. Sorrow is not itself repentance; repentance is the work of that sorrow.

lessons.title: The Gospel That Must Be Believed
lessons.summary: This is the Gospel. This is what one must believe to be saved: that Jesus is the Christ, that by His death our sins are forgiven, in His blood, and in His resurrection, the promise of eternal life.

lessons.title: Justified Before Men – James 2
lessons.summary: We are justified before God by our faith and justified before men by our works. Paul is writing of justification before God in grace, while James is writing of justification before man, by doing good works in faith.

lessons.title: The Blood Atonement
lessons.summary: Only the blood of a holy God offered in our place and sprinkled on the mercy seat can atone for our sin and justify us before God. That is the only propitiation.

lessons.title: Adopted Sons and Heirs
lessons.summary: We who are saved by grace through faith are adopted as sons of God, heirs to His promise and the Kingdom of Heaven. We become sons of God when we are born again, but the adoption is at the resurrection, the day of redemption.

pictures.title: Abide in the doctrine of Christ
pictures.alt: A dark silhouette of a robed figure walking along a shore toward a pale sun. Text quotes 2 John 1:9-11 KJV: whosoever abideth not in the doctrine of Christ hath not God; receive him not into your house, neither bid him God speed.

Below: James 1:2-4, 'My brethren, count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations...'.

pictures.title: All things were created by him and for him

A heartlight.org logo is in the corner.
